+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.47.5	water deep enough to swim in	The commentary gives س ب ح the literal gloss “swim in water”; Ezekiel's temple river grows until it is deep enough for swimming, adding a sacred, measured current as a concrete water-motion image.

+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.32.16	separated herds in a moving caravan	The commentary arranges horses and camels by those ahead and behind; Jacob sends successive animal droves ahead with space between them, adding a staged caravan whose order serves a plan.

+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.2	awakening to everlasting life	The commentary says the later life is better and more enduring; Daniel describes sleepers in the dust awakening, some to everlasting life, supplying an explicit resurrection horizon.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.13	rest, then rise at the end of days	The commentary makes the afterlife the latter stage and calls it lasting; Daniel is told to go to his rest and rise for his allotted inheritance at the end of days, giving that sequence a personal resurrection outcome.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.31.24	Moses completes a written book	The commentary says the message is in earlier scrolls and names Moses; Deuteronomy says Moses finishes writing the words of the Torah in a book, a concrete Mosaic witness to written scripture.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.31.26	book of the law deposited as witness	The commentary names Moses among the sources of the earlier scrolls; Moses orders the written book of the law placed beside the covenant ark as a witness, adding its preserved public role.
+medium	tevrat	motif	Berakhot 17a	World to Come beyond rivalry	The commentary extends a race's front and rear positions to the afterlife; Berakhot portrays the World to Come without eating, trade, jealousy, hatred, or competition, with the righteous enjoying God's presence, limiting the race image to this life's sequence.
+strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.116.17	thanksgiving and calling on God's name	The commentary says the worshipper remembers the Lord's name and prays; the psalm joins a thanksgiving offering with calling on YHWH's name, adding a concrete liturgical form of that pairing.
+medium	tevrat	motif	4 Ezra 7	the present age and the future age	The commentary contrasts the near life with the better, lasting life after it; in chapter 7 Uriel compares the hard passage of the present age with the future age's reward. Verse divisions vary by edition, so this is cited at chapter level.
+medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.25.34	birthright exchanged for one meal	The commentary condemns preferring the near life over what follows; Esau trades his birthright for food and despises it, a concrete choice of immediate satisfaction over a later inheritance.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.16	Esau sells inheritance for a meal	The commentary's 87:16–17 contrast is immediate preference against later good; Hebrews names Esau as one who sold his birthright for a single meal, turning the Genesis episode into an ethical warning about short-term choice.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.17	later regret cannot recover the blessing	The commentary says the early choice may not win the final outcome; Hebrews recalls that Esau later sought the blessing with tears but could not reverse what happened, adding the consequence of a short-sighted exchange.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.16	Abraham's company desires a better country	The commentary names Abraham in the former scrolls and says the later life is better; Hebrews says the patriarchs desired a better, heavenly country, making Abrahamic faith look beyond the present homeland.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.25	Moses rejects fleeting pleasure	The commentary criticizes preferring this world's life; Hebrews says Moses chose mistreatment with God's people over the temporary enjoyment of sin, a direct choice against near pleasure.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.11.26	Moses looks toward the reward	The commentary says what follows is better than the first gain; Hebrews says Moses valued reproach above Egypt's treasures because he looked toward the reward, making future recompense govern present choice.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.5.46	Moses' writing read as forward-looking	The commentary says the message is in former scrolls and names Moses; Jesus says Moses wrote about him, a New Testament interpretation that gives Mosaic scripture a forward-looking witness.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.12.25	losing present life to keep eternal life	The commentary says people prefer worldly life over the better later one; Jesus says one who loves life loses it, while one who gives up life in this world keeps it for eternal life, directly reversing that preference.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.11.2	prayer begins by hallowing the Father's name	The commentary says the worshipper remembers the Lord's name and then prays; Jesus teaches prayer that opens by asking that the Father's name be hallowed, joining divine-name devotion to the prayer itself.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.13.30	last and first at the kingdom's table	The commentary says the first arrival is not necessarily the winner; after describing entry into God's kingdom, Jesus says some who are last will be first and first last, placing the reversal in an eschatological gathering.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.24.13	endurance to the end	The commentary's horse holds strength for the latter stretch; Jesus says the one who endures to the end will be saved, making final persistence decisive.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.9.27	discipline or risk disqualification	The commentary says an early position does not guarantee the final win; Paul disciplines his body lest, after preaching to others, he himself be disqualified, adding the possibility that even a runner can fail at the end.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.2.5	athlete crowned only under the rules	The commentary links the race order to a later prize; Paul says an athlete is not crowned unless competing lawfully, adding that position and desire alone do not secure the outcome.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Tim.6.17	rich urged not to hope in uncertain wealth	The commentary says people prefer worldly life; Paul tells the rich not to set hope on uncertain wealth but on God, a specific correction to misplaced present security.
+strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Tim.6.19	treasure stored for the future life	The commentary calls the later life better and lasting; Paul says the rich should store up treasure as a foundation for the future and take hold of the life that is truly life, spelling out present action for future gain.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.1.12	crown of life after endurance	The commentary says the horse preserves its running for later; James blesses the one who endures trial and promises the crown of life, making the reward follow sustained endurance.
+medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.1.4	imperishable inheritance reserved in heaven	The commentary says the afterlife is more enduring; Peter describes an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven, adding a reserved future possession.

*** End Patch";
